<!-- pr-reviewer: 16450307a34d91c565d16a28a370b7357ddbd024 -->
Needs changes before merge.

The milling controls use the active setup's machine kind. Non-mill controls remain enabled. WCS changes use the existing command. The generation refusal remains unchanged.

I reviewed the code against current upstream main's AGENTS.md. I tested the trial merge locally with upstream/main at a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504. The merge had no conflicts. No GitHub runner was used.

Local results:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | Passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui` | 861 passed, 1 failed, 6 ignored |
| `boundary` | 3 passed |
| `boundary_picks` | 6 passed |
| `sinker_setup` | 2 passed |
| `tap_hand` | 3 passed |
| `theme_files` | 14 passed |
| `waterjet_tool` | 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| WCS tests after mutation restoration | 9 passed |

The library failure was `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`. A separate local run failed for the same reason:

```text
egui headless run failed: no graphics adapter: software adapter: No suitable graphics adapter found; noop support not compiled in, vulkan support not compiled in, metal found no adapters, dx12 support not compiled in, gl support not compiled in, webgpu support not compiled in; hardware adapter: No suitable graphics adapter found; noop support not compiled in, vulkan support not compiled in, metal found no adapters, dx12 support not compiled in, gl support not compiled in, webgpu support not compiled in
```

This machine cannot complete that graphics test. I do not classify this environment failure as a code defect.

Safety review: The stack changes the WCS rotation transform through #1684. I checked the composition order and the oblique-axis tests. No golden files changed.

I repeated two mutations in the local review worktree:

- Set `turn_row`'s `enabled` value to `true`. The milling test failed with `Turn X+ must be disabled on a milling setup`.
- Set `tilted_mill` to `false`. The milling test failed with `expected tilted-WCS warning naming Level`.

I restored the source. All nine WCS tests then passed. No mutation remains in the source.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs:43`: Add before and after screenshots to this PR's body. Show the milling controls and the warning for an existing tilted milling WCS. This UI change has no screenshots in its body. Store the images only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Link them from the PR body. Do not commit images or review evidence to this PR's branch.

Note: #1684 remains open. Keep the stated merge order. The screenshots in #1684 do not show this PR's milling guard.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the latest review's only requested change. The PR body now has before and after screenshots of the same milling setup with an existing 15° WCS roll. They show the X/Y milling controls and the new tilted-WCS warning. The images are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch at 48a03f38de7f937d4ff4409979e733115adbc432.

The screenshot-link pin passed. Removing the screenshot section made it fail; restoring it made it pass. Both remote PNGs match the captured files. The existing behavior pin is `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is red only because `headless_run_succeeds` cannot find a graphics adapter. This is the environment failure already identified in the review. All other selected tests passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Head: 16450307a34d91c565d16a28a370b7357ddbd024. It is unchanged because this finding required only screenshots and a PR body update. Plain push reported everything up to date. No images, capture code, logs, or review evidence were committed to the PR branch. The PR remains a draft. The stated #1684 merge order is preserved.

Please re-review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 16450307a34d91c565d16a28a370b7357ddbd024 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge, after #1684.

The later evidence comment permits this review of the same head. I opened both images linked in the PR body. They show the same milling setup with 15 degrees of roll. The before image shows enabled X/Y controls and no warning. The after image shows disabled X/Y controls and the warning that names Level and Part alignment. This meets the only request in my earlier review. I withdraw that request.

I checked the code against AGENTS.md on upstream/main at 42438238cd7900b5d413b9b84720e0a691401d04. The local trial merge had no conflicts. The guard uses the active setup's machine kind. Non-mill controls remain enabled. WCS changes use the existing command. The generation refusal is unchanged.

All checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2099`. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | Passed |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | Passed |
| UI library, from `crates/ui` | 882 passed, 6 ignored |
| `boundary` | 3 passed |
| `boundary_picks` | 6 passed |
| `sinker_setup` | 2 passed |
| `tap_hand` | 3 passed |
| `theme_files` | 14 passed |
| `waterjet_tool` | 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |
| WCS tests after source restoration | 9 passed |

The headless graphics test passed on this trial merge. No pixel snapshot tests were run.

Safety review: The stack changes WCS rotation math through #1684. I checked the local-axis composition and the oblique-axis tests. No golden files changed. I repeated these two mutations myself:

- Set `turn_row`'s `enabled` value to `true`. The milling test failed: `Turn X+ must be disabled on a milling setup`.
- Set `tilted_mill` to `false`. The milling test failed: `expected tilted-WCS warning naming Level`.

I restored the source. All nine WCS tests then passed. The worktree has no source changes.

Requested before merge: none.

Note: #1684 is still open. Merge it first, as stated in the PR body. The screenshots are linked from the fork's images branch. The PR contains no screenshots or review evidence.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
